_meta.purpose: The information gap, as data. Every question here is referenced by id from the docs, the dashboard pages and COORDINATION.md, so the same list cannot drift in two places.
_meta.rule: Known = verified against an official source or a live API read, with the link. Missing = not knowable from this repository without you or a credential. No item is marked resolved by inference.

questions.question: What should “culture” mean for this dashboard, given Kalshi publishes no Culture category?
questions.why_it_matters: It decides which events appear at all. A wrong choice silently drops or adds entire rows on the leaderboard.
known: The official taxonomy from GET /search/tags_by_categories contains: AI, Business, Climate and Weather, Commodities, Companies, Crypto, Economics, Elections, Entertainment, Financials, Health, Mentions, Politics, Science and Technology, Social, Sports, World (plus Test, harrison-test and a null name). No Culture.
Entertainment, Mentions and Social are the three published buckets whose series look cultural (awards, charts, person-of-the-year, game releases).
KXTIME (Time Person of the Year) was returned by tag search, not by any category filter, and is used as the current anchor.
questions.missing: Which of those you consider in scope, and whether Sports-adjacent pop events (e.g. box office, video game releases) belong.
questions.how_to_find_out: Open the taxonomy read, pick the categories, then edit data/topics.json topics[id=culture].selectors and re-run scripts/collect.py.
questions.suggestion: Keep Entertainment + Mentions + Social, label the column 'Entertainment/Mentions/Social (no Culture category)' rather than renaming it Culture, and treat any series found only by prefix as provisional.

questions.question: “Gas prices” — retail pump price, or the oil/gas commodity contracts the exchange actually lists?
questions.why_it_matters: If you meant pump prices, the topic may have no live markets to track, and the leaderboard row would be permanently empty.
known: Commodities carries the tag 'Oil & Gas'; Economics carries 'Oil and energy'. Both were read from the live taxonomy endpoint.
The selector Commodities+Oil & Gas returns crude/natural-gas series (KXWTIW weekly strikes, Brent, heating oil, TTF gas).
No series whose title references retail or pump gasoline appeared in any capture in this session.
KXWTIW weekly strikes currently have bid 0.0000 / ask 1.0000 with volume_fp 0.00 — a real empty book, not a missing read.
questions.missing: Whether an empty-book proxy is acceptable, or the topic should be dropped until a pump-price series exists.
questions.how_to_find_out: python3 scripts/kalshi_api.py series Economics "Oil and energy" and compare against the Commodities selector; search the demo site UI for 'gasoline'.
questions.suggestion: Track the energy complex (WTI/Brent/nat-gas) under the label 'Gas & energy prices', and re-check the Economics selector each run so a new retail series is picked up automatically.

questions.question: Which dollar definition should the leaderboard rank on?
questions.why_it_matters: There is no dollar-volume field, so any ranking is a modelling choice; the choice changes the order of every row.
known: GET /markets and GET /series publish volume_fp / volume_24h_fp in CONTRACTS, and notional_value_dollars per contract (1.0000 on every market sampled).
The tape (GET /markets/trades) gives count_fp plus yes_price_dollars and no_price_dollars per fill, so dollars must be summed from fills.
Both parties in a trade pay the same price, so pricing the taker's own side is the least assumptive choice.
Current formula: sum over trades of count_fp x (yes_price_dollars if taker_outcome_side=='yes' else no_price_dollars).
questions.missing: Whether you prefer (a) taker-side notional, (b) YES-leg notional only, or (c) contracts.
questions.how_to_find_out: Compare the two formulas on the same capture: scripts/aggregate_capture.py prints taker-side; scripts/analyze.py prints YES-leg notional. Both numbers are on the site.
questions.suggestion: Keep taker-side notional as the ranking key (it matches what money actually moved), and always show contracts next to it so a $1-notional assumption is visible.

questions.question: Can a demo-environment API key be provided, so the portfolio and execution paths run against the real account?
questions.why_it_matters: This is the single blocker on requirements (d) and (e): portfolio performance and executed trades need signed /portfolio/* calls.
known: The code path exists and is exercised end to end in paper mode: trade_engine -> portfolio -> analyze -> site.
Signing is RSA-PSS-SHA256 (or Ed25519) over timestamp+METHOD+path-including-/trade-api/v2, with KALSHI-ACCESS-KEY / -TIMESTAMP / -SIGNATURE headers.
Demo keys are created in the demo account only and never work on production, and vice versa.
GET /portfolio/balance needs the read::portfolio_balance scope; fills/positions need their own scopes.
The engine hard-refuses to send orders to a non-demo host.
questions.missing: A key id and a no-passphrase private PEM, supplied via environment variables — never via chat.
questions.how_to_find_out: Create the key at https://demo.kalshi.co/ under API keys, then export KALSHI_API_KEY_ID and KALSHI_PRIVATE_KEY_PEM_PATH for the runner.
questions.suggestion: Run scripts/kalshi_api.py auth-check first: it verifies signing against a read-only endpoint before anything can mutate the account.

questions.question: Which fee model should P&L use for demo — the published schedule, or only the API's own fee_cost?
questions.why_it_matters: A wrong fee turns a profitable ledger into a loss and vice versa.
known: Every sampled series reports fee_type 'quadratic' with fee_multiplier 1; one variant family includes maker fees (quadratic_with_maker_fees / quadratic_with_combo_maker_fees) and some are flat.
Fills carry fee_cost directly, which is authoritative for that fill.
The official fee schedule PDF is the only published description of the quadratic curve.
Portfolio code therefore uses fill.fee_cost only, and the paper engine labels its estimate 'illustrative_fee_not_a_quote'.
questions.missing: Your call on whether to model fees for planning (pre-trade estimate) in addition to using actual fee_cost for reporting.
questions.how_to_find_out: Open the fee schedule PDF and compare its curve against fee_cost values observed on real demo fills once Q-04 is unblocked.
questions.suggestion: Keep reporting on actual fee_cost only; add a pre-trade estimator as a separate, clearly-labelled field, never folded into P&L.

questions.question: Should this project ever touch production, or stay demo-only permanently?
questions.why_it_matters: Production means real money, real settlement and real orders; the repo currently hard-refuses it by design.
known: Hosts differ (demo: external-api.demo.kalshi.co / demo-api.kalshi.co; production: external-api.kalshi.com / api.elections.kalshi.com) and keys are not interchangeable.
Kalshi warns demo prices and behaviour may not reflect real markets.
trade_engine.py raises OrderError if --execute is used against a non-demo base.
questions.missing: Your decision on scope. Default is demo-only, permanently.
questions.how_to_find_out: No research needed — this is a policy choice.
questions.suggestion: Keep demo-only. If production is ever wanted, use a separate deployment and a separate key, and never a shared execute path.

questions.question: Include multivariate (MVE) combo markets in the ranking, or keep them excluded?
questions.why_it_matters: MVE combos currently sort to the top of /markets with zero volume and is_provisional set, which would corrupt a naive leaderboard.
known: GET /markets returns provisional multivariate combos unless mve_filter=exclude is used; they carry volume_fp 0.00 and is_provisional.
GET /events documents that multivariate events are excluded from its response entirely.
Combos settle under collateral_return_type MECNET or DIRECNET, which is not the plain-binary payout model.
questions.missing: Whether you want combo exposure tracked as its own section.
questions.how_to_find_out: python3 scripts/kalshi_api.py markets --mve-filter include --limit 5 and inspect is_provisional plus collateral_return_type.
questions.suggestion: Keep them out of the ranking; add a separate, clearly-labelled combos page only if asked.

questions.question: Is the demo REST API CORS-open, so a GitHub Pages deployment can call it directly from the browser?
questions.why_it_matters: It decides whether the deployed site is genuinely live or necessarily snapshot-backed.
known: Kalshi publishes no CORS statement anywhere in the docs index; no Access-Control-Allow-Origin behaviour is documented.
The site therefore attempts a live read at load time, and falls back to the collector snapshot with a visible banner when it fails.
The local dev_server.py bridge exists for the case where the browser is blocked: it proxies same-origin and can add signatures.
questions.missing: A definitive answer for the demo host from a browser on the Pages origin, which this sandbox cannot test (no egress to kalshi.co).
questions.how_to_find_out: Open the deployed site with ?mode=live and read the banner; or run curl -i -H 'Origin: https://<pages-host>' against /exchange/status and inspect the CORS headers.
questions.suggestion: Assume blocked, ship the bridge, and re-test after deploy; the fallback path is already built and labelled.

questions.question: What polling budget is acceptable for unauthenticated public reads?
questions.why_it_matters: Unauthenticated limits are documented as separate and stricter, with no published numbers; over-polling is the fastest way to 429 the dashboard.
known: Rate limits use a token bucket: default 10 tokens per request class, separate Read and Write budgets, a 3-second burst window at Basic/Advanced read levels, and no Retry-After header on 429.
Public unauthenticated traffic has its own undocumented limits.
The docs state REST responses are cached briefly, so sub-second polling returns stale data anyway.
GET /series ignores a limit parameter and has no cursor, so a full sweep is one large response, not a paged loop.
questions.missing: A budget you are comfortable with for continuous collection (interval and pages per run).
questions.how_to_find_out: Watch X-RateLimit-* headers on responses during a test run; that is the only empirical way.
questions.suggestion: Default the UI to 15 s with 8 tape pages, keep any cron at 1-5 minutes, and back off on 429 without retrying immediately.

questions.question: How long should raw captures be retained in the repository?
questions.why_it_matters: Every published number must stay traceable to a raw response, but tape captures grow fast and this repo is served from the same branch.
known: data/raw/trades-capture.json holds 28 verbatim trade records (6.9 KB) and is the sole input to every derived dollar figure.
site/data/ is generated at build time by scripts/publish_snapshot.py, so published artifacts are reproducible from data/.
Cumulative patchset size in this environment is capped, which argues against logging every page of tape.
questions.missing: Your retention preference (per-run file, daily rollup, or nothing but the last capture).
questions.suggestion: Keep the newest capture per day plus any capture that backs a published claim; drop the rest in the same commit that publishes.

questions.question: Which horizon should the seconds axis cover, given the API has no sub-minute history?
questions.why_it_matters: The requirement asks for a seconds-granular X axis, which the candlestick API cannot answer; the workaround has a hard memory bound.
known: period_interval accepts only 1, 60 or 1440 minutes, and a response is capped at 5,000 periods.
A seconds axis therefore exists only as client-sampled data, starting when you open the page; it is labelled 'client-sampled' and never merged into candle series.
The WebSocket trade/ticker channels are the only real-time source, and every WS handshake requires a signature.
questions.missing: How long a sampling window to keep in the browser (currently 900 points per market at 5 s = 75 minutes).
questions.how_to_find_out: Judge it in use on the dashboard; the constant is one line in site/assets/api.js.
questions.suggestion: Keep 5 s sampling for the watchlist only, and use the bridge with WS for anything denser.

questions.question: Should the order book ladder keep showing only bids plus an implied ask, or persist derived asks as their own field?
questions.why_it_matters: The ask side is a derivation, not a read; presenting it as data would be a fabricated value.
known: orderbook_fp returns yes_dollars and no_dollars as [price_dollars, count_fp] arrays, ascending, bids only, best last.
A YES bid at X is equivalent to a NO ask at 1 - X, which is how the ladder prints the ask side.
depth=N controls how many levels come back; the ladder uses the raw bids and shows the derivation inline.
questions.missing: Whether you want the derived ask stored in data/ at all, or shown only in the UI.
questions.how_to_find_out: No research needed; both options are one-line differences in collect.py.
questions.suggestion: Show it in the UI labelled 'implied', never write it into the published data as if it were an API field.

questions.question: Should paper trades be counted in performance reporting at all?
questions.why_it_matters: A paper fill looks exactly like a real one in a table; only its label distinguishes them.
known: The engine stamps mode on every record and portfolio.load_paper only ingests entries with mode='paper' AND a filled response.
Every affected KPI on the site carries a paper tag, and the ledger sets simulated=true.
Real reporting uses /portfolio/fills; that path is untested because no key exists.
questions.missing: Whether you want paper rows in the same tables with labels, or excluded entirely and shown only on a separate page.
questions.suggestion: Keep them in the same tables, labelled, because the point of this project is exercising the full pipeline; the label plus the mode field makes mixing impossible to miss.

questions.question: Is the demo tape's synthetic character acceptable for demonstrating the ranking pipeline?
questions.why_it_matters: If the demo feed is synthetic, the ranking code is validated but the numbers are not market truth.
known: Within ~0.2 s of the tape window, 120 fills printed in sizes like 5555.55 and 1851.85 contracts — round repeating fractions, not organic order flow.
Kalshi's own docs state demo prices and behaviour may not reflect real markets.
The pipeline itself is host-agnostic: pointing the collector at production changes only the base URL.
questions.missing: Whether you want the site to keep a permanent 'demo data, possibly synthetic' banner, or drop it once production reads are available.
questions.how_to_find_out: Compare one hour of /markets/trades on demo against the same window on production when a key exists.
questions.suggestion: Keep the banner. The dashboard's value here is the method; hiding the provenance would oversell it.
